Definition: of Hebrew origin (H3876); Lot, a patriarch:--Lot.
BiblicalUsage: Lṓt belongs to Lot, the patriarch, and the Bible does not let it pass unnamed. In Luke 17:28, "Likewise also as it was in the days of Lot"; and in Luke 17:29, "But the same day that Lot went out of Sodom it rained fire and brimstone from heaven". In 2 Peter 2:7, "And delivered just Lot".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Lot is the righteous man vexed by the filthy — delivered, but only just, and his wife remembered as a warning, and the days of Lot will come again, with fire falling the same day he went out. My position is that I will not linger in Sodom; I will go out when God says go.
